title: Use a torque wrench correctly
summary: Set, use and store a click-type torque wrench so bolts end up at the value on your spec sheet.

steps.text: Pick a wrench whose range covers the value. Readings are least accurate in the bottom 20% of the scale.
Unlock the handle and turn it until the scale reads the value in N·m. To convert, 1 kgf·m is about 9.8 N·m.
Make sure the thread is clean and the fastener is snugged down by hand or with a normal wrench first.
Hold the wrench by the handle grip only and pull smoothly at a right angle to the wrench.
Stop the instant it clicks. Don't pull again to double-check; that adds extra torque.
steps.caution: Never use a torque wrench to loosen bolts. It throws off the calibration.

steps.text: After use, wind the setting back to the lowest value and store it in its case.
